question: Which part of the Constitution of India deals with ‘Citizenship’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part II of the Indian Constitution deals with Citizenship, covering Articles 5 to 11. (नागरिकता — भाग II)

 

• Part II defines who became a citizen of India at the commencement of the Constitution (26 January 1950), covering citizenship by domicile, migration from Pakistan, and by registration for persons of Indian origin residing abroad.

 

• Subsequent acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship is governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955, enacted by Parliament under the power given by Article 11.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part III of the Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35); Part IV deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51).

 

• Part I deals with the Union and its Territory (Articles 1-4).

 

NOTE

 

• Part I (Option 1): Deals with the Union and its Territory, not citizenship.

 

• Part III (Option 2): Deals with Fundamental Rights, not citizenship.

 

• Part IV (Option 3): Deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy, not citizenship.

question: In a symport:
option_1: a molecule moves across a membrane independent of other molecules
option_2: both molecules cross the membrane in the same direction
option_3: both molecules cross the membrane in the opposite direction
option_4: a molecule moves across a membrane dependent of other molecules
solution_text:
The correct answer is both molecules cross the membrane in the same direction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A symport (co-transporter) is a membrane transport protein that carries two different molecules/ions across the cell membrane simultaneously in the same direction. (सहपरिवहन — समान दिशा में गति)

 

• Symport is a form of secondary active transport: the movement of one substance down its concentration gradient (commonly Na⁺) is coupled to, and drives, the movement of a second substance against its gradient, both moving the same way across the membrane.

 

• A classic example is the sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) found in intestinal and renal epithelial cells, which moves Na⁺ and glucose into the cell together.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Transport of two substances in opposite directions across a membrane is called an antiport (e.g., the Na⁺/H⁺ exchanger, or indirectly the Na⁺/K⁺ pump).

 

• Transport of a single molecule/ion, unaccompanied by movement of another species, is called a uniport (e.g., GLUT glucose transporters).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Describes a uniport, where one molecule crosses the membrane independently of any other — not a symport, which by definition involves two coupled molecules.

 

• Option 3: Describes an antiport, where two molecules move simultaneously but in opposite directions, the reverse of a symport.

 

• Option 4: Vaguely gestures at coupled transport but omits the defining feature of a symport — that both molecules move in the same direction — so it does not correctly define the term.

question: The Braj festival in ________ is held every year for two days in the Shukla Paksha of the Phalgun month, a few days before Holi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Braj Festival is a two-day cultural festival celebrated every year at Bharatpur, Rajasthan, in the Shukla Paksha of the Phalgun month, just a few days before Holi. (ब्रज महोत्सव — भरतपुर, राजस्थान)

 

• It is organised by the Rajasthan Tourism Department and showcases folk dances, music, and the colourful traditions of the Krishna-worshipping Braj culture, celebrating the arrival of spring alongside Holi festivities.

 

• The festival features processions, folk performances, and cultural programmes centred on Radha-Krishna legends, reflecting Bharatpur's cultural affinity with the wider Braj Bhoomi region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan hosts several other notable fairs and festivals, including the Pushkar Fair, Teej, Gangaur, and the Desert Festival of Jaisalmer.

 

• The core Braj region associated with Krishna's legends (Mathura, Vrindavan, Gokul, Barsana) lies mainly in Uttar Pradesh; Bharatpur in neighbouring Rajasthan celebrates its own Braj Festival owing to its cultural and geographical proximity.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 2): Known for festivals such as Kullu Dussehra and the Minjar Mela, not the Braj Festival.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Known for festivals such as the Khajuraho Dance Festival, not the Braj Festival.

 

• Haryana (Option 4): Known for festivals such as the Surajkund Mela, not the Braj Festival.

question: The Kailasha temple at Ellora near Aurangabad in Maharashtra was built by a king from the _____ Dynasty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtrakuta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kailasa (Kailasanatha) Temple at Ellora, near Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), Maharashtra, was built in the 8th century CE under the Rashtrakuta dynasty, chiefly credited to king Krishna I. (कैलाश मंदिर, एलोरा — राष्ट्रकूट वंश)

 

• It is the largest monolithic rock-cut temple in the world, carved vertically downward out of a single basalt rock, dedicated to Lord Shiva and designed to represent his abode, Mount Kailasa.

 

• The Ellora Caves (34 caves comprising Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain shrines) were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rashtrakutas ruled from their capital at Manyakheta (Malkhed) in present-day Karnataka; notable rulers include Dantidurga, Krishna I, and Amoghavarsha I.

 

• Amoghavarsha I is credited with the Kannada literary classic *Kavirajamarga* and is known for his long, stable reign.

 

NOTE

 

• Pratihara (Option 2): The Pratiharas ruled from Kannauj in northern/western India and are known for structures like the Teli ka Mandir at Gwalior, not the Kailasa temple.

 

• Gurjara Pratihara (Option 3): The fuller name of the same dynasty as Option 2; not associated with Ellora's Kailasa temple.

 

• Chandella (Option 4): The Chandelas built the famous temple complex at Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh, not at Ellora.

question: Where and when was India’s first Senior National Archery Championship held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi, 1973.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first Senior National Archery Championship was held in Delhi in 1973, the same year the Archery Association of India (AAI) was formed (8 August 1973), following the reintroduction of archery to the Olympic Games in 1972. (तीरंदाजी चैंपियनशिप — दिल्ली, 1973)

 

• The Archery Association of India is the national governing body for the sport in India and is affiliated to World Archery.

 

• Since that first edition, the Senior National Archery Championship has continued as the apex domestic archery competition, with later editions co-organised with bodies such as the SAI and, more recently, sponsors like NTPC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Notable Indian archers who have represented the country at the Olympics and World Championships include Deepika Kumari, Atanu Das, and Jyothi Surekha Vennam.

 

• The NTPC Senior National Archery Championship is the modern, sponsor-named continuation of this annual national event.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai, 1973 (Option 2): Incorrect city — the first edition was held in Delhi.

 

• Chennai, 1975 (Option 3): Both the city and the year are incorrect.

 

• Delhi, 1975 (Option 4): Correct city but incorrect year — the championship was first held in 1973, not 1975.

question: Which of the following persons was sworn in as chief of the Central Information Commission of India in November 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Heeralal Samariya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Heeralal Samariya, a retired IAS officer, was sworn in as the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) of India on 6 November 2023. (केंद्रीय सूचना आयोग — हीरालाल सामरिया)

 

• He took oath along with two new Information Commissioners, administered by the then President of India, in the presence of senior government functionaries.

 

• The Central Information Commission (CIC) was established under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, and is the apex body for hearing appeals and complaints regarding denial of information under the Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CIC consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to 10 Information Commissioners, appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister.

 

• The Central Information Commission has its headquarters in New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Bimal Julka (Option 1): A former Chief Information Commissioner who held office earlier (2018-2020), not the one sworn in as chief in November 2023.

 

• Yashovardhan Azad (Option 2): A former Information Commissioner, not the Chief Information Commissioner sworn in November 2023.

 

• Divya Prakash Sinha (Option 3): Not the person sworn in as chief of the CIC in November 2023.

question: Which of the following committees had recommended the inclusion of a chapter on the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India and stressed that the citizens should become conscious that, in addition to the enjoyment of rights, they also have certain duties to perform?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swaran Singh Committee (1976).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) was constituted by the Congress government to recommend amendments to the Constitution, and it proposed the inclusion of a separate chapter on Fundamental Duties, stressing that citizens must be conscious of their duties alongside their rights. (स्वर्ण सिंह समिति — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• On the committee's recommendation, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 inserted a new Part IVA containing Article 51A, which originally listed 10 Fundamental Duties (a 11th was added later by the 86th Amendment, 2002).

 

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was inspired in part by their inclusion in the erstwhile USSR's Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are enumerated under Article 51A in Part IVA of the Constitution and are non-justiciable, i.e., not enforceable by courts.

 

• The 11th Fundamental Duty (a parent/guardian's duty to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

NOTE

 

• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (Option 1): Related to recommendations on Panchayati Raj / community development, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• JR Varma Committee (Option 2): Related to mutual fund/securities regulation matters, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Ashok Mehta Committee (Option 3): Related to Panchayati Raj institutions, not Fundamental Duties.

question: Which of the following is NOT an alignment option for text in a cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justified.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In common spreadsheet applications (e.g., MS Excel), the standard, directly available horizontal text-alignment options for a cell are Left, Center, and Right. (सेल संरेखण — Left, Center, Right)

 

• Justified alignment, which evenly spaces text to align with both the left and right margins, is a feature associated with word processors (e.g., MS Word) for paragraph text, not a standard basic alignment button for spreadsheet cell text.

 

• Because Left, Center, and Right are the three options typically offered as the basic alignment choices for cell text, Justified is the one that is NOT among them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Spreadsheet software also offers vertical alignment options for cell content, such as Top, Middle, and Bottom.

 

• Word processors like MS Word use Justify to stretch each line of a paragraph (except the last) so that it aligns evenly at both the left and right margins.

 

NOTE

 

• Center (Option 1): A standard, commonly available alignment option for cell text.

 

• Right (Option 2): A standard, commonly available alignment option for cell text.

 

• Left (Option 4): A standard, commonly available alignment option for cell text.

question: The Thomas Cup is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badminton male.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Thomas Cup is the premier international men's team badminton championship, organised by the Badminton World Federation (BWF). (थॉमस कप — पुरुष बैडमिंटन)

 

• It was first held in 1948-49 and is named after Sir George Alan Thomas, a former president of the International Badminton Federation, who donated the trophy.

 

• India won the Thomas Cup for the first time in 2022, defeating Indonesia in the final, held in Bangkok, Thailand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The equivalent women's team badminton championship is the Uber Cup.

 

• The mixed-team badminton championship is the Sudirman Cup.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton female (Option 1): The women's team badminton event is called the Uber Cup, not the Thomas Cup.

 

• Tennis female (Option 2): The Thomas Cup is a badminton event, not a tennis event.

 

• Tennis male (Option 3): The Thomas Cup is a badminton event, not a tennis event; men's team tennis is contested for the Davis Cup.

question: Which of the following is the most dominant species of the Tropical Deciduous Forests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Teak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Teak (Tectona grandis) is the most dominant and commercially valuable tree species of India's Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon) Forests, prized for its strong, durable timber. (सागौन — उष्णकटिबंधीय पर्णपाती वन)

 

• Tropical Deciduous forests are found in regions receiving 70-200 cm of annual rainfall and are India's most widespread forest type, further divided into Moist Deciduous and Dry Deciduous forests.

 

• Teak grows predominantly in the moist deciduous forests of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, and parts of Uttar Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sal (Shorea robusta) is another dominant species of the moist deciduous forests, especially in the eastern parts of the country (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal).

 

• Dry deciduous forests, receiving less rainfall, are dominated by species like tendu, palas, amaltas, khair, and axlewood.

 

NOTE

 

• Mulberry (Option 1): The food plant of the silkworm, cultivated commercially for sericulture, not a dominant tropical deciduous forest species.

 

• Rubber (Option 2): Associated with equatorial/tropical evergreen plantation regions (e.g., Kerala), not tropical deciduous forests.

 

• Coconut (Option 3): A coastal/tropical crop, not a dominant species of tropical deciduous forests.

question: Which of the following song did AR Rahman record with Michael Jackson?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ekam Satyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A.R. Rahman recorded the song “Ekam Satyam” together with Michael Jackson, blending Sanskrit chanting with Jackson's vocals. (एकम सत्यम — ए.आर. रहमान और माइकल जैक्सन)

 

• The collaboration originated around the making of Jackson's unfinished project and was later associated with a compilation informally referred to as *Ekam Satyam* / *One Truth*, reflecting a spiritual, unifying theme.

 

• A.R. Rahman is a globally acclaimed Indian music composer, winner of two Academy Awards (Oscars), two Grammy Awards, and a BAFTA, for his work on *Slumdog Millionaire* (2008).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A.R. Rahman is also known for iconic scores such as *Roja*, *Bombay*, *Lagaan*, *Rockstar*, and *Jai Ho* (from *Slumdog Millionaire*), and holds honours including the Padma Bhushan (2010).

 

• Michael Jackson, known as the “King of Pop,” was an American singer, songwriter, and dancer, one of the most influential figures in the history of popular music.

 

NOTE

 

• You are my destiny (Option 2): Not a Rahman-Jackson collaboration; not associated with this pairing.

 

• The Oracle (Option 3): Not a Rahman-Jackson collaboration.

 

• Infinity Love (Option 4): Not a Rahman-Jackson collaboration.

question: __________ is one of the well-known schemes sponsored by the Union Government of India. It was launched in November 2015 with the aim of rescuing the country’s ailing electricity distribution companies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY) was launched by the Ministry of Power in November 2015 to financially and operationally turn around debt-ridden state-owned power distribution companies (DISCOMs). (उदय योजना — विद्युत वितरण कंपनियों का पुनरुद्धार)

 

• Under UDAY, participating state governments took over 75% of their DISCOMs' debt (as of September 2015) and issued bonds to cover it, easing the interest burden on the distribution companies.

 

• The scheme aimed to reduce Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses, close the gap between the average cost of supply and revenue realised, and improve the operational efficiency of DISCOMs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS) focuses on strengthening sub-transmission and distribution networks in urban areas.

 

• The Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY), launched in 2014-15, focuses on rural electrification and feeder separation.

 

NOTE

 

• Integrated Power Development Scheme (Option 1): Targets urban power distribution infrastructure, not the financial turnaround of DISCOMs.

 

• One Nation, One Grid (Option 2): Refers to the integration of India's regional power grids into a single national grid, not a DISCOM rescue scheme.

 

• Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (Option 3): A rural electrification scheme, not the DISCOM financial-turnaround scheme launched in November 2015.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE about the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) of India?

i. One of the main objectives of the Zones Act was promotion of exports of goods and services.

ii. The Government of India announced the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) Policy in the year 2011.

iii. The SEZ Rules provided for different minimum land requirement for different classes of SEZs.

Which of the above statements is/are FALSE?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Special Economic Zones (SEZs) Policy was actually announced by the Government of India in April 2000, not 2011, making Statement ii false. (विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र नीति — अप्रैल 2000)

 

• Statement i is correct: The SEZ Act, 2005 (which came into force in February 2006) explicitly aims at the promotion of exports of goods and services, among other objectives like generation of additional economic activity and employment.

 

• Statement iii is correct: The SEZ Rules, 2006 prescribe different minimum land-area requirements for different classes of SEZs — e.g., a minimum of 1,000 hectares for a multi-product SEZ, lower limits for sector-specific SEZs, and no minimum land requirement for IT/ITES SEZs (only minimum built-up area applies).

 

• Since only Statement ii is factually incorrect, the correct answer to “which statement(s) is/are FALSE” is “Only ii.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• SEZs enjoy fiscal incentives such as duty-free import/procurement, and were, for a period, eligible for income-tax exemptions under Section 10AA of the Income Tax Act (phased out for new units after FY 2019-20).

 

• India's SEZ policy was influenced by China's success with SEZs; India's first EPZ (precursor to SEZs) was set up at Kandla, Gujarat, in 1965.

 

NOTE

 

• Only i and ii (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement i is actually a true statement, not false.

 

• Only ii and iii (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement iii is actually a true statement, not false.

 

• Only iii (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement iii is true (differential land norms do exist), while it is Statement ii, not iii, that is false.

question: Which of the following tribes does NOT live in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maasai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maasai are an indigenous ethnic group inhabiting parts of Kenya and northern Tanzania in East Africa, and do not live in India. (मासाई जनजाति — केन्या और तंजानिया)

 

• The Tharu, Gond, and Santhal are all indigenous tribal communities living within India (and in the Tharu's case, also in the Terai region of Nepal).

 

• The Gonds are among the largest tribal groups of India, found mainly in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, and adjoining states, while the Santhals are concentrated in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Maasai are widely known for their distinctive customs, red shuka clothing, and cattle-herding pastoral lifestyle in the African Great Lakes region.

 

• India's tribal population, as per Census data, is concentrated in central India (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand) and the North-East.

 

NOTE

 

• Tharu (Option 2): An indigenous tribal community living in the Terai region of India (Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar) and Nepal.

 

• Gond (Option 3): A major tribal community of central India, particularly Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Maharashtra.

 

• Santhal (Option 4): A major tribal community of eastern India, particularly Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar.

question: How can we add text to a slide in MS-PowerPoint?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Textbox.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS-PowerPoint, text is added to a slide by inserting a Textbox (via Insert → Text Box) or by typing into the placeholder text boxes already present in a slide's layout. (टेक्स्ट बॉक्स — MS-PowerPoint)

 

• A Textbox is a movable, resizable container into which the user can click and type text anywhere on the slide, independent of the predefined placeholders.

 

• Slide layouts in PowerPoint typically come with placeholder boxes for a title and content/body text, which are themselves a form of text box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Notes pane/Notes Page view in PowerPoint is used to add speaker notes for the presenter, which are not displayed to the audience during the slideshow.

 

• Other PowerPoint text-related features include WordArt for stylised text and SmartArt for text-based diagrams.

 

NOTE

 

• Note box (Option 1): Not a standard PowerPoint feature name for adding slide text.

 

• Dialogue box (Option 2): A general UI element used for settings/options, not the way text is added to a slide.

 

• Notes page (Option 3): Used for adding speaker notes for the presenter's reference, not the content displayed on the slide itself.

question: Who was the first to use the term 'horsepower' that refers to the power produced by an engine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Watt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• James Watt, the Scottish engineer famed for improving the steam engine, coined the term “horsepower” in the late 18th century to compare the output of his steam engines with the power of draft horses. (अश्वशक्ति (हॉर्सपावर) — जेम्स वाट)

 

• One horsepower is defined as approximately 746 watts in the SI system, a unit still commonly used today to express the power of engines and motors.

 

• Watt's contributions to the steam engine were so significant that the SI unit of power, the “watt,” is named in his honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• James Watt also introduced the concept of the Watt steam engine (1776), a major improvement over Thomas Newcomen's earlier design, which was pivotal to the Industrial Revolution.

 

• The unit “watt” was officially adopted by the Second Congress of the British Association for the Advancement of Science in 1889.

 

NOTE

 

• John Dalton (Option 1): Known for proposing modern atomic theory, not the term “horsepower.”

 

• Amedeo Avogadro (Option 2): Known for Avogadro's law/Avogadro's number in chemistry, not the term “horsepower.”

 

• Albert Einstein (Option 3): Known for the theory of relativity, not the term “horsepower.”

question: Which of the following is NOT a moon of Jupiter?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Triton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Triton is the largest moon of Neptune, not a moon of Jupiter. (ट्राइटन — नेपच्यून का उपग्रह)

 

• Callisto, Europa, and Ganymede, along with Io, are the four large Galilean moons of Jupiter, discovered by Galileo Galilei in 1610.

 

• Ganymede is the largest moon in the entire Solar System, even bigger than the planet Mercury.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Europa is of particular scientific interest because of the strong evidence for a subsurface liquid-water ocean beneath its icy crust, making it a key target in the search for extraterrestrial life.

 

• Triton is notable for its retrograde orbit around Neptune, suggesting it was a captured Kuiper Belt object rather than having formed alongside the planet.

 

NOTE

 

• Callisto (Option 2): One of the four Galilean moons of Jupiter, incorrectly listed here as the answer since it genuinely IS a moon of Jupiter.

 

• Europa (Option 3): One of the four Galilean moons of Jupiter.

 

• Ganymede (Option 4): One of the four Galilean moons of Jupiter, and the largest moon in the Solar System.

question: Under the discretionary power of which Article of the Indian Constitution did the SC of India recognise sex work as a profession?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 142.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Supreme Court of India, exercising its special discretionary power under Article 142 of the Constitution, held in its 2022 ruling that sex work is a “profession” and that sex workers are entitled to dignity and equal protection of law. (अनुच्छेद 142 — सेक्स वर्क को “पेशा” मान्यता)

 

• Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any order necessary for “complete justice” in any matter pending before it, and such orders are enforceable throughout India.

 

• This ruling came from a bench headed by Justice L. Nageswara Rao, directing police and other authorities not to interfere with consenting adult sex workers and to treat them with dignity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 141 provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India.

 

• Article 143 empowers the President to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion on questions of law or fact of public importance.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 143 (Option 2): Concerns the President's power to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion, not the sex-work ruling.

 

• Article 141 (Option 3): Concerns the binding nature of Supreme Court law on all courts, not the specific discretionary power invoked in this ruling.

 

• Article 140 (Option 4): Empowers Parliament to confer supplementary powers on the Supreme Court by law; not the article invoked in this ruling.

question: Which of the following pairs of state and folk dance is correctly paired?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab – Bhangra dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhangra is a vigorous, energetic folk dance native to Punjab, traditionally performed by men during the harvest festival of Baisakhi, accompanied by the dhol drum. (भांगड़ा — पंजाब)

 

• The other pairings in this question are mismatched: Garia/Goria is actually a folk dance of Tripura, Ghoomar is a folk dance of Rajasthan, and Bihu is a folk dance of Assam.

 

• Bhangra has today grown into a globally popular dance form, performed at weddings, festivals, and even fused with contemporary music genres worldwide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Punjab's other folk dance, performed by women, is the Giddha.

 

• Well-known state–folk dance pairs include Rajasthan – Ghoomar, Assam – Bihu, and Gujarat – Garba/Dandiya Raas.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana – Garia or Goria dance (Option 2): Incorrect; Garia (Goria) is a folk dance of Tripura, not Haryana. Haryana's own folk dances include the Phag dance and Dhamal.

 

• Kerala – Ghoomar dance (Option 3): Incorrect; Ghoomar is a folk dance of Rajasthan, not Kerala. Kerala's folk dances include Theyyam and Kaikottikali.

 

• Gujarat – Bihu dance (Option 4): Incorrect; Bihu is a folk dance of Assam, not Gujarat. Gujarat's own folk dances include Garba and Dandiya Raas.

question:
On the basis of highest population growth rate (Census, 2011), select the option that arranges the following states in descending order.

A) Bihar

B) Arunachal Pradesh

C) Meghalaya
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, B, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, the decadal population growth rate (2001-2011) of these states was highest for Meghalaya (about 27.8%), followed by Arunachal Pradesh (about 26.0%), and then Bihar (about 25.4%). (जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर 2011 — मेघालय सर्वाधिक)

 

• Arranged in descending order of growth rate, the correct sequence is Meghalaya > Arunachal Pradesh > Bihar, i.e., C, B, A.

 

• Several North-Eastern and eastern states recorded relatively high decadal growth rates in the 2001-2011 Census, while some southern states (e.g., Kerala) recorded much lower growth rates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, India's overall decadal population growth rate (2001-2011) was 17.64%, the lowest recorded since independence up to that point.

 

• Nagaland was a notable exception among North-Eastern states, recording a negative population growth rate in the 2001-2011 decade.

 

NOTE

 

• A, B, C (Option 2): Incorrect order — Bihar actually had the lowest growth rate of the three, not the highest.

 

• C, A, B (Option 3): Incorrect order — Arunachal Pradesh's growth rate was higher than Bihar's, so Arunachal Pradesh (B) should rank above Bihar (A).

 

• B, C, A (Option 4): Incorrect order — Meghalaya's growth rate was the highest of the three, so it should rank first, not Arunachal Pradesh.

question: Former Union Minister _________ from Manipur was awarded Padma Shri in 2023 by the Union government for his contribution in public affairs in the last four decades.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thounaojam Chaoba.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thounaojam Chaoba Singh, a veteran political leader from Manipur, former Union Minister of State and former Deputy Chief Minister of Manipur, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 for his contribution to Public Affairs spanning over four decades. (पद्म श्री 2023 — थौनाओजम चाओबा, मणिपुर)

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred by the President of India on the recommendation of the Padma Awards Committee, recognising distinguished contributions in various fields.

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day (26 January) and are given across categories including art, social work, public affairs, science, and sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are given in three categories in descending order of importance: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

 

• Padma Awards are conferred in various disciplines/fields such as art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, and civil service.

 

NOTE

 

• Thokchom Radheshyam Singh (Option 1): Not the Manipur-origin former Union Minister awarded the Padma Shri 2023 for public affairs described in this question.

 

• Yumnam Joykumar (Option 3): A Manipuri politician and former IPS officer, but not the person described in this question.

 

• Okram Ibobi Singh (Option 4): A former Chief Minister of Manipur, but not the former Union Minister awarded the Padma Shri 2023 described in this question.

question: National income at constant prices means:
option_1: income estimated for next year prices
option_2: income estimated at base year prices
option_3: income estimated at current year prices
option_4: income estimated at any year prices
solution_text:
The correct answer is income estimated at base year prices.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National income at constant prices (also called “real national income”) is the value of goods and services produced, measured using the prices prevailing in a fixed base year, thereby eliminating the effect of price changes (inflation) over time. (स्थिर मूल्यों पर राष्ट्रीय आय — आधार वर्ष की कीमतें)

 

• By holding prices constant at base-year levels, this measure isolates the real change in the physical volume of output, making it possible to compare economic growth across years without the distortion caused by inflation.

 

• In contrast, national income at current prices (“nominal national income”) uses the prevailing prices of the year in which output is produced, so it reflects both changes in output and changes in prices.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's base year for national accounts was revised to 2011-12 by the Central Statistics Office (now National Statistical Office) in January 2015.

 

• The ratio of nominal to real GDP, expressed as an index, gives the GDP deflator, a broad measure of price-level changes in the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Income estimated for next year prices (Option 1): Not a recognised concept in national income accounting.

 

• Income estimated at current year prices (Option 3): This describes national income at current prices (nominal income), the opposite of constant-price (real) income.

 

• Income estimated at any year prices (Option 4): Too vague and imprecise; constant-price income specifically uses a fixed base year's prices, not “any year.”

question: Who composed the music of the patriotic song ‘Maa Tujhe Salaam’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AR Rahman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The patriotic song “Maa Tujhe Salaam” was composed and sung by A.R. Rahman, released as part of his 1997 album “Vande Mataram”, produced to mark 50 years of India's independence. (माँ तुझे सलाम — ए.आर. रहमान)

 

• The album became one of the most iconic patriotic music releases in India, with “Maa Tujhe Salaam” becoming especially popular for its energetic remix version.

 

• A.R. Rahman is renowned globally for his film scores and has won numerous awards, including two Academy Awards and two Grammy Awards for *Slumdog Millionaire* (2008).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A.R. Rahman has composed for numerous acclaimed Hindi and Tamil films, including *Roja*, *Bombay*, *Dil Se*, *Lagaan*, *Rockstar*, and *Jai Ho*.

 

• He has been honoured with India's civilian awards, including the Padma Bhushan (2010).

 

NOTE

 

• Anu Malik (Option 1): A prominent Bollywood music director, but not the composer of “Maa Tujhe Salaam.”

 

• Shankar Mahadevan (Option 2): A renowned playback singer and part of the Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy trio, but not the composer of this song.

 

• Himesh Reshammiya (Option 3): A well-known Bollywood music director and singer, but not the composer of this song.

question: Where did the indigenous sport ‘Gatka’ originate from?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gatka is a traditional Sikh martial art that originated in Punjab, in which practitioners use wooden sticks (simulating swords) to simulate armed combat. (गतका — पंजाब की पारंपरिक युद्ध कला)

 

• Gatka has deep roots in Sikh military tradition, historically used for training warriors, and remains an important part of Sikh cultural and religious celebrations, especially around Vaisakhi and Gurpurabs.

 

• The Gatka Federation of India promotes the sport, which has also been included as a demonstration/competitive event in some National Games editions in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian indigenous martial arts include Kalaripayattu (Kerala), Silambam (Tamil Nadu), and Thang-Ta (Manipur).

 

• Gatka performances often accompany Sikh religious processions such as Nagar Kirtans.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 1): Not the state of origin of Gatka.

 

• Manipur (Option 2): Home to the martial art Thang-Ta, not Gatka.

 

• Jammu and Kashmir (Option 4): Not the state of origin of Gatka.

question: The birthday of ________ is celebrated as the International Day of Non-Violence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Day of Non-Violence is observed every year on 2 October, the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi, in recognition of his philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and peaceful resistance (Satyagraha). (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अहिंसा दिवस — 2 अक्टूबर, महात्मा गांधी)

 

• The day was established by a United Nations General Assembly resolution adopted on 15 June 2007, reaffirming the universal relevance of the principle of non-violence.

 

• 2 October is also observed as a national holiday (Gandhi Jayanti) within India itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahatma Gandhi led India's freedom struggle through movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), the Civil Disobedience Movement / Dandi March (1930), and the Quit India Movement (1942).

 

• He is popularly known as the “Father of the Nation” in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhimrao Ambedkar (Option 1): His birthday (14 April) is observed as Ambedkar Jayanti, not the International Day of Non-Violence.

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 3): His birthday (31 October) is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day), not the International Day of Non-Violence.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 4): His birthday is observed as part of literary/cultural commemorations, not the International Day of Non-Violence.
